pinterest.title: Why Do We Have Bridesmaids? From Classical Athens to Queen Victoria's Twelve in White
pinterest.description: Why do we have bridesmaids? So a bride has people she trusts beside her, helping before and during the ceremony. In classical Athens, bridesmaids danced at wedding feasts. In 1840 Queen Victoria had twelve bridesmaids, all eldest daughters of peers, dressed in white to a design she sketched herself. Our guide follows the bridesmaid tradition from then to now, and how to choose your own attendants.

pinterest.title: Maid of Honour or Matron of Honour? The Difference Is Marriage, Not Rank
pinterest.description: The maid of honour is the most important bridesmaid. A matron of honour is a married woman in the same lead role, so the difference is marriage, not rank. Both lead the bridal party and the duties are the same. Many couples now skip the labels: a person of honour can be a brother or a best friend. Some couples name two, sharing the speech and the jobs, and agree early who does what.

pinterest.title: Bridesmaids at a Destination Wedding: Questions to Talk Through Before Anyone Books
pinterest.description: Asking someone to be a bridesmaid abroad is asking for their leave, their travel and several days of their year. Ask early and in person, and give them room to say no. Talk through who covers flights and accommodation, who covers hair and make-up, how many days attendants are expected and whether partners and children can come. Then build in a free afternoon so friends can see the place.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Why do we have bridesmaids? Because a wedding is easier, and happier, with people you trust beside you. A bridesmaid helps the bride before and during the ceremony, and that simple job has carried the role through centuries of change.

Attendants at weddings are very old. In classical Athens, bridesmaids danced at wedding feasts, and at a Roman wedding the matron of honour linked the right hands of the bride and groom.

In 1840 Queen Victoria had twelve bridesmaids, all eldest daughters of peers, dressed in white to a design she sketched herself. They carried her 18-foot train, and Prince Albert designed their gift: an eagle-shaped turquoise brooch.

Today the role goes to the people who have been there all along. A sister, a school friend, a brother, a partner's cousin. Maid or matron of honour, the difference is marriage, not rank, and a bridesman can stand on the bride's side just as easily.

Marrying abroad? Ask early and in person, talk openly about who covers travel and time off before anyone books, and give friends room to say no.

newsletter.blurb: We have bridesmaids so a bride has people she trusts beside her, before and during the ceremony. Our new guide follows the role from the wedding feasts of classical Athens to Queen Victoria's twelve bridesmaids in white in 1840, then turns to the choices in front of you now: maid or matron of honour, how many to ask, bridesmen and mixed parties, and how to ask friends to travel for a wedding abroad, with the questions to talk through before anyone books.
